newsitem.title: UK: UK's Co-operative Bank H1 profits surge 24 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Co-operative Bank H1 profits surge 24 pct.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Bank, which will only invest in ethically or environmentally friendly businesses, posted record results on Wednesday as first half pretax profits surged 24 percent to 25.1 million stg.
Average customer deposits jumped 28 percent to 2.3 billion stg and average customer lending rose 16 percent to 1.9 billion.
The Co-operative Bank said a charge for doubtful debt fell 10 percent to 11.8 million stg and added that net interest income rose 20 percent, mainly due to higher customer balances.
"Despite intensive competition the Bank maintained the net interest margin (up 0.1 percent) and increased customer balances which indicate greater market share," it said in a statement.
Managing director Terry Thomas said the bank's "competitive prices and high quality customer service" were the main factors attracting customers.

The bank, which announced its third successive record half year results, says it has the cheapest ever credit card with an APR of 7.9 percent and has also introduced a new savings account paying a top rate of 6.0 percent per year.
Operating income rose 14 percent and expenses for the period were 16.2 million stg, due to the accelerated promotional activity and the expansion of distribution and service facilies.
